First listed: 2026-10-30 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Anthropic’s Growth is Slowing: Is AI Capex Next? | The Weekly Wrap](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z-pClpi6eTY) - 2026-10-30
- [Substack: Anthropic’s Growth is Slowing: Is AI Capex Next?](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/anthropics-growth-is-slowing-is-ai) - 2026-10-30

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The October 30 wrap links weaker AI financing and several earnings disappointments to possible capex deceleration. Anthropic growth and compute ratios support a narrow slowdown observation, but the token-maxing cause is unproven. Microsoft identifies delayed capacity delivery and Amazon reports accelerating AWS growth, important counterweights to the bearish cycle inference. Eisman clarifies fixed-coupon versus new-debt cost and presents conditional 2027 power constraints.

Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.

- [ServiceNow Q3 2026 results and outlook](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371526000095/erq3fy262.htm) (2026-10-28): Q3 non-GAAP EPS $1.00. Q4 cRPO growth guidance 18.5%, but subscription revenue guidance 22.5%-23% reported and 21.5% constant currency. cRPO slowdown is not identical to immediate revenue contraction.

Prior-year Anthropic investment gains largely explain lower net income. Operating income rose from $17.4 to $28.1 billion, AWS grew 39%, and TTM FCF was negative $42.4 billion after AI capex.
- [Microsoft FY27 Q1 earnings conference call](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/Investor/events/fy-2027/earnings-fy-2027-q1) (2026-10-28): Azure grew 48%. Capex $45.2 billion reflected delayed third-party capacity deliveries. Management said demand exceeded supply, guided Q2 capex above $50 billion and acceleration in fiscal H2. The shortfall does not by itself establish weaker end demand.

### 029. A secondary bond yield rising above its coupon does not immediately raise the cash interest payment on an existing fixed-rate bond.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 23:09-23:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z-pClpi6eTY&t=1389s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning: The issuer pays the contracted coupon times face value regardless of the secondary price. Yield changes because the buyer's price and expected return change. This corrects the earlier shorthand that existing debt cost rose immediately.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

## Framework and tools

- Separate sequential growth from absolute growth.
- Compare revenue with compute expense, but do not treat the ratio as a complete profit model.
- Distinguish GAAP EPS from investment gains and adjusted measures.
- Distinguish fixed coupon cash payments from market funding cost.
- Separate capex delivery delays from end-demand weakness.
- Treat viewer field reports as hypotheses requiring broader validation.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Anthropic quarterly revenue, compute expense and efficiency ratio table
- Compute commitment totals by supplier
- Earnings, guidance and share-reaction comparisons
- CoreWeave secondary yield versus coupon
- Grid connection lead times

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman solo, quoting two viewers. A Doomberg promotional excerpt and sponsor message are excluded.
- Local MLX Whisper transcription has no speaker diarization and garbles names.
- Recorded October 29 for October 30 publication.
- Introductory Doomberg audio is a promotional excerpt, not adopted as a new Eisman forecast.
- Kalshi sponsored promotion is excluded.
- Opening montage repeats body claims.
- Viewer Joseph and Wayne assertions are attributed separately.
